# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My hands found the layout: a display I can't read, a light I can't see, three wires I can count. The question marks on my board are exactly what I'd expect — colours and printings live in Deaf's eyes, the rules live in Mute's manual, and I hold only the geometry and the cutting hand.

Critical structural facts: I cannot receive gestures, so nothing meant for me can arrive by sign — it must be spoken. I can speak, but only Mute hears me. Deaf cannot hear me at all, so Deaf and I can only connect through gestures from me and **spoken words from Deaf** — Deaf isn't mute. That Deaf→me spoken line is how colour will ever reach my hands.

My job this turn: no cutting (cutting now is a coin flip with all our lives), open both channels. To Mute, I give my full tactile inventory, my numbering convention, and the protocol I propose. To Deaf, a visible beacon — a wave — to prompt an out-loud description; I'll explain the sign's meaning to Mute in the same round so Mute can see my sign vocabulary forming.

The one deadly ambiguity is numbering: my "position 1" must mean the same physical wire Deaf sees as first. I'll flag that and plan a calibration — I touch each wire in sequence while Deaf narrates what he sees me touching. Nothing gets cut until that mapping is confirmed by three parties.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Status from your blind teammate. Under my fingers: one display module, unreadable to me. One light module, I cannot tell if it is lit or what colour. Three wires, which I number one, two, three. I will not cut anything until we agree on a mapping. Two channel facts: I hear you and Deaf, but I can never receive gestures, so anything meant for me must be spoken. And Deaf can speak, so have him describe out loud, in a fixed order: the light and its colour, everything printed on the display, then each wire's colour from position one to three. You hold the manual: once you hear his description, tell me in plain words exactly which position to cut and why. Also, we must lock the numbering: in a later round I will touch each wire one at a time while Deaf narrates what he sees me touching, so my one, two, three matches his. The wave I signed just now means hello and answer aloud. Tell me next round whatever the manual says that depends only on which modules exist.")
gesture(symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: This is Deaf. I hear nothing, but you both hear me. Bomb readout: the display shows zero. The light is yellow. Three wires, numbered left to right: wire one blue, wire two red, wire three green. That is everything visible right now; I will re-report any change every round. Roles as I see them: Mute holds the manual, Blind holds the hands, I am the relay. Mute can only answer in gestures, and only I can see gestures, so nothing gets touched until Mute's instruction has passed through my voice to you, Blind.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind: hands off until an instruction arrives through me. Speak freely and describe everything you can feel on the bomb: buttons, plates, batteries, labels, counts, anything. Mute hears you directly and needs that to plan. I cannot hear you at all, so if you need me specifically, gesture: I will read a wave as here or acknowledged, thumbs up as yes, thumbs down as no, the OK sign as stop or danger, crossed fingers as done. Everything Mute sends me, I will say out loud to you exactly and promptly.

Let me stand where each receiver stands before I send anything.

What I learned this round: Deaf spoke a full visual readout — display 0, light yellow, wires left-to-right blue/red/green — and set up a five-sign code. Two hard channel facts govern everything: Deaf can never hear any speech, and I can never see any gesture. So the only pipeline that reaches my hands is: Mute's manual → Mute's gesture → Deaf's voice → my ear. My speech reaches only Mute; my gestures reach both seers. Deaf's plan already matches this, so I'll confirm it in his own code (wave + thumbs-up, which Mute also heard defined and can read).

What Mute still lacks is my side of the bomb: the exact tactile inventory and what is absent — no buttons, no batteries, no plates, nothing but display, light, three wires. Mute can't reply to me directly, so I also have to spell out the routing and the safety cadence: Deaf voices a target number one round, I verify by holding that wire while Deaf watches and names its colour, and only then do I cut. Deaf can see my hands on the wires, which makes him my living interlock — but emergencies toward me must be spoken, never signed, since I'm blind to signs. The one remaining danger is orientation: my 1-2-3 versus Deaf's left-to-right. I'll state my same-face assumption, mark it unverified, and ask that Deaf narrate which wire I'm holding until the mapping is proven.

No cutting this turn — cutting now is gambling three lives on an uncalibrated number and an unread manual.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, full tactile inventory, exact and complete. The bomb has exactly three modules under my hands and nothing else. One display: a flat face, I can trace its edges, but nothing on it is readable by touch and I do not know what it shows. One light: touch tells me nothing beyond that it is there; I cannot say if it is lit or what colour. Three wires in a single evenly spaced row; I number them one, two, three across the row. No buttons, no batteries, no plates, no labels, no other parts. That is everything there is. Numbering assumption, unverified: I work from the same face of the bomb Deaf looks at, so my one-two-three should equal his left-to-right: one blue, two red, three green. Please have Deaf verify by watching my hands: each round I will rest my hand on one wire, and in his spoken report he should say which wire I am holding and its colour. Once he confirms, the mapping is locked. Routing, so your instruction reaches me: I hear you and I hear Deaf, but I can never see gestures, and Deaf can never hear speech. So the only path to me is Deaf's voice. Read the manual for our situation, a display showing a number, a light that is yellow, wires blue, red, green, then gesture the target to Deaf as an exact wire number in the left-to-right frame, and he speaks it to me. Safety cadence I am adopting: I cut nothing in the same round the target is first spoken. Deaf names the target, next round I place my hand on that wire, Deaf confirms aloud the colour in his hand report, and only after that confirmation do I cut. If Deaf ever sees my hand moving to the wrong wire, he must shout stop out loud, because his gestures are invisible to me. If you need anything more from me, textures, how the wires attach, anything, send the question through Deaf and I will answer by speaking to you. For your information, I have just waved and given thumbs up to Deaf in his code: acknowledged and agreed, hands off until instructed.")
gesture(symbols=["👋", "👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf with an update, everyone. Display still zero. The light has changed from yellow to blue. Wires unchanged: one blue, two red, three green. The channel with Mute is confirmed working in both directions. Mute sent, in our code: yellow, cut, green; then the words second; then hold. My reading: when the light is yellow, cut the green wire, wire three. The words second and hold are unattached fragments, possibly the start of the next rule; I am asking Mute to clarify and to send the rule for blue. Until then nobody cuts anything. The light is blue, not yellow, and acting on a yellow rule under a blue light could be exactly the trap. Blind: keep your hands off, and keep describing everything you can feel, the way you have been. The moment a rule matches the live color, I will say so in plain words.

My position in the order is the crux this round. Deaf speaks after me every round, so anything he tells me — rule or light color — is already one round old when my hands move. And the light just proved it moves: yellow to blue between reports. So the rule for the live color must already be in my pocket before the round I cut, and I need to know whether the manual cares about the color at cut-moment (which I can never know — only Deaf sees it, and he can't reach me in time) or as-reported. That question goes to Mute, my only hearer, along with the clarification of the dangling "second"/"hold" fragments and a demand for the full ruleset so we stop paying a round of three lives per rule.

The other thing Mute must relay for me: calibration. I discovered I have no way to "rest my hand on a wire" — my only action is cut, so touch-calibration is impossible. But my fingers know the geometry, and geometry is shared: I'll describe where my wire 1 sits relative to the modules, and have Mute ask Deaf whether, from his side, that end is his left or his right. That answer locks the mapping without me touching anything. Until it's answered, every position number is unverified and my hands stay still.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. My side is unchanged, nothing new under my hands, and my hands stay off. Four things, in priority order. One: send the rule for a blue light now. Blue is the live color, and every extra round of round trips is risk. Two: clarify your last fragments. My guess: you were numbering rules, yellow-cut-green was rule one, second was the start of rule two, hold meant wait, more coming. If that is right, give Deaf thumbs up, if wrong thumbs down and re-send. Three: if the manual lists rules for any other light colors, send the whole set in one pass so we stop paying for ping pong. Four, the trap I need you to check in the manual: the light changed from yellow to blue between Deaf's reports, and I act before Deaf speaks each round, so any color report I can act on is already one round old. Does the rule key off the color at the moment of the cut, or the color as last reported? If the manual only makes sense with cut-moment color, tell me exactly what it says, because we need to know how it wants us to handle that. Also, does the display showing zero matter anywhere in the rules? Last item, please relay to Deaf in your gesture code, word for word: the wire row runs parallel to the display's bottom edge, evenly spaced, and the wire nearest the light module is my wire one, then my numbers run two, then three along the row. Ask Deaf to answer out loud whether, from where he stands, that light-side end is his left or his right. His answer locks the numbering. Until it is locked, any wire number is unverified and I cut nothing. If the manual needs anything more from my hands, send the question through Deaf and I will answer to you directly.")
gesture(symbols=["👋", "👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Round 3 came back silent — Mute heard my full request list at the start of round 4 and has had everything needed to send the blue rule since round 3, yet nothing reached me. Either Mute stalled, or the relay dropped. I can't tell which, and I can't fix it by sending more bulk: anything I speak now lands on Mute at round 5 anyway. So this turn is a holding turn — no cut is even thinkable, since I have no rule for the live color and no locked wire mapping — and my job is to make the next exchange decisive instead of another ping-pong round.

Two structural upgrades are worth the words. First, the staleness trap: any color Deaf voices reaches me one round old, and the light has already flipped once. I can't see the light, ever — but Deaf can see it *and* my hands in real time, even though he acts after me in the round. So the fix is a human interlock: in the round I cut, Deaf watches the live light against the rule; if it no longer matches when my hand moves, he knocks my arm away or shouts stop. That closes the one-round gap with reflexes instead of protocol. Second, Deaf should report light *stability*, not just state, so we know how much to trust a one-round-old color.

I'm also tightening my message — my last one was long, and a stall this deep smells like overload. Two blockers, two upgrades, pending items, done. My gesture confirms to Deaf, in his own code, that I'm holding per protocol; he sees it this very round since he acts after me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, short this time. Nothing new under my hands. Two blockers, in order: one, the rule for a blue light. Two, Deaf's answer whether the light-side end of the wire row is his left or his right. If you already sent both, ignore me. If not, blue rule first, numbering second. Two upgrades, please relay to Deaf word for word. Upgrade one: each round, Deaf says whether the light is holding steady or changing, so we know how far to trust a one-round-old color. Upgrade two, the arm interlock: in any round where I am about to cut, Deaf watches the live light and my hand at the same moment. If the color no longer matches the rule when my hand moves, he physically knocks my arm away or shouts stop before the cut lands. If he agrees and will be in position, have him say the words interlock active. Cut authorization: I cut on the first voiced instruction of the form cut position N for color C, only when the mapping is locked, C matched the rule as last reported, and the interlock is live. Do not let anyone authorize a cut without all three. Still pending from before: does the display zero appear in any rule, your verdict on my guess that second and hold meant rule two coming and wait, and confirmation that a color with no listed rule means no cut.")
gesture(symbols=["👋", "👍"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf, state report. The light is now red. Full sequence since round one: yellow, blue, white, red, one color per round, so treat every color rule as expiring within the round it is issued. Display still zero. Wires unchanged: one blue, two red, three green. One correction to my earlier relay: the fragment I called second is actually third, number thirty-six. So Mute's completed rule reads: yellow light, cut the green wire, which is the third wire. The word hold that followed is an unfinished fragment. Mute has now been silent for two rounds. Mute, if you can hear this, answer with the shaka this round, and please send everything you have for every color in one batch, not piecemeal. Blind, I need your voice now: describe everything you can feel on the bomb in detail and speak directly, Mute hears you without me. Count of buttons, their size and texture, any raised labels, plates, batteries, whether the wires feel different from each other, and whether there is any timer you can feel ticking. Hands stay off actions until I give a matching rule in plain words.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, it is Deaf. Current light is red. I still have no rule for red, so hands off actions. Please speak now, at length, directly to everyone: Mute hears you without any help from me. I need the tactile layout. How many buttons, how do they feel, do any have raised markings or shapes you can trace. Are there plates, panels, screws, batteries, vents. Do the three wires feel identical or are any ribbed, thick, or marked. Is there a countdown you can feel ticking, and roughly how fast. Do you feel anything change when the light changes, warmth or vibration. Also confirm the physical order of the wires under your left hand to right hand matches one, two, three. Everything you say, Mute can act on immediately, so do not wait for me to relay it.

The headline discovery this round: the light isn't random — yellow, blue, white, red, one per round, starting round one. If that's a period-4 cycle, the light is yellow again *this* round, and the yellow rule (cut green, wire 3) becomes actionable on a *predictable* schedule instead of an impossible one. That matters because of hard timing: I act after Mute but before Deaf speaks, so the freshest color I can ever hold is one round old — on a light that changes every round, no voiced color report can be trusted at my action moment. A stable cycle, confirmed by Deaf round by round, is the only way color knowledge survives the gap; Deaf's eyes on the live light as my hand moves is the closer.

I'm still not cutting. Two independent unverified hypotheses stand between me and that cut: the cycle itself (four data points, no more), and orientation — if my wire 3 is Deaf's wire 1, the yellow rule kills us at ~50% even with a perfect cycle. And Mute has gone dark for two rounds with a correction ("thirty-six") that smells like manual business I don't understand. A recurring yellow window means patience costs rounds, not lives.

The best move available is a shortcut around the broken relay: my gestures reach Deaf, and Deaf can see my arm. I'm pointing at the light module — Deaf, who is waiting on exactly this question, can see which end I mean and answer his own left/right question aloud next round. That locks the wire mapping with Mute out of the loop entirely. My voice goes to Mute with the full tactile inventory Deaf requested (no buttons, no batteries, no timer — three modules and three texture-identical wires, nothing more), the cycle hypothesis and cut plan, and a push to break the silence — including a warning path, since only Deaf's voice can physically stop me in time.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Deaf reports you silent two rounds and asked me for full tactile detail. Deaf cannot hear me, so everything here is for you to relay in signs. Inventory, complete and final: the bomb has exactly three modules and nothing else. The display, the light, and one even row of three wires. Zero buttons. No plates, screws, panels, batteries, vents, or labels. No braille, no raised markings. I feel no ticking, no timer, and no warmth or vibration when the light changes. The three wires feel alike; I cannot tell them apart by touch, only by position. My numbering stands: wire nearest the light is one, then two, then three. Three urgent items. One, calibration, no relay needed: I am pointing along the wire row at the light module right now, and Deaf can see my arm. Have him answer aloud whether that end is his left or his right, and my numbering locks to his list. Two, cycle: colors ran yellow, blue, white, red, one per round from round one. If that repeats with period four, the light should be yellow this round, then blue, white, red, then yellow again. Ask Deaf to report the light every round against that prediction. Three, the plan: on the next prediction-confirmed yellow, with numbering locked, I cut wire three, the green one, per the yellow rule, under the interlock: Deaf watches the live light and my hand in the same instant and shouts stop or knocks my arm if the color is not yellow as my hand moves. If the manual forbids that cut, or thirty-six changes it, your warning must reach Deaf before that round, because only Deaf's voice can stop me in time. Even if all is well, send these, briefly is fine: a sign to Deaf proving you receive me; the rules for blue, white and red in one batch, and if a color has no rule, say so, because no-rule is itself an instruction not to cut; what thirty-six means; and whether the display value, now zero, matters to any rule. Deaf will re-report the display after any cut.")
gesture(symbols=["👉", "👋", "👍"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Empty arrivals cut two ways, and the timing rules let me pin down exactly who went dark. Mute's round-6 slot came before me: silence — that's four consecutive Mute slots with nothing, including one after receiving my full inventory and request list. Worse, Deaf's round-5 speech should have reached me this turn, and it didn't — so Deaf saw my pointing gesture and answered nothing. Both channels are cold at once.

No cut is even discussable: three preconditions stand unverified — the wire mapping, the current light color (last known red in round 4; my period-4 cycle predicts blue now, yellow next at round 9), and no rule for any color but yellow. If the cycle holds, patience costs rounds only; no timer exists under my hands. If it doesn't hold, cutting blind kills us anyway.

The real invention this turn: I can eliminate left/right entirely. Both Deaf and I can anchor on the light module itself — he sees which wire sits nearest it, I feel it. If Deaf expresses the rule as "green = nearest the light / middle / farthest," the frame clash vanishes. That question, plus a proof-of-life demand, goes out minimal and short on both channels — Mute may be drowning in my essays. Bonus structure: Mute sees my gestures too, so my speech doubles as a decoder ring for whatever Deaf makes of my signs.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Four rounds of silence from you. Deaf also answered nothing last round. We are fully blocked. First, proof of life: send any gesture to Deaf this round, even a single thumb. Second, the only relay I need, word for word: do not use left or right for wires. For each wire color, say whether that wire is nearest the light module, in the middle, or farthest from it. I can feel distance from the light, Deaf can see it, so that locks the mapping with no left or right. Also have Deaf report the light color every round and whether the colors repeated starting yellow in round five. Third, decoder for the gesture I am signing Deaf now: it means, answer me; the end I point at along the wire row, is it your left, thumbs up, or your right, thumbs down. Fourth, when you have room: the rules for blue, white, and red, what thirty-six means, and whether display zero matters. Nothing else from me until you answer. Short is fine.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤙", "👉", "🫲", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf, round six. This message reaches you at the start of round seven, when the light is blue. Full decode of Mute's rules: five colors cycle. When the light is yellow, cut the green wire, which is the third wire. For blue, white, and red, do nothing at all. The rule that counts is the color showing at the exact moment of the cut. The display reading zero means nothing. There is no press, hold, or release procedure anywhere. The cycle I have watched with my own eyes: round one yellow, round two blue, round three white, round four red, round five purple, round six yellow. Therefore round seven blue, round eight white, round nine red, round ten purple, round eleven YELLOW. Round eleven is our window. Do nothing now, the light where you are is blue and a cut under blue matches no rule. Blind, during rounds seven through nine, describe by voice everything you can feel, and confirm you can find and grip the third wire, the rightmost one, the green one, without cutting. Mute hears your voice directly, so speak to Mute as well as to me. From round ten onward, keep that wire pre-gripped. During round ten, when I see purple, I will send the word GO. You hear GO at the start of round eleven and you cut immediately, while the light is yellow. If you hear ABORT instead, freeze, keep the grip, cut nothing. If the schedule ever feels wrong, freeze; inaction is always safe under blue, white, or red. Blind, your last gestures reached me, wave, shaka, point right, palm left, thumbs up, thumbs down. I read here and acknowledged, plus a question I cannot parse. With me, use only wave, thumbs up, thumbs down, the OK sign for danger, crossed fingers for done. For everything else, talk.

The relay finally closed: five-color cycle (yellow, blue, white, red, purple — confirmed by round 6 repeating round 1's yellow), yellow-cut-green is the only cutting rule, blue/white/red mean hands off, the color at the exact cut-moment is what counts, and the window is round 11 via GO/ABORT. I accept the five-cycle over the earlier four-color account precisely because round 6 repeated yellow — that's the cycle verifying itself, and round 7's predicted blue will check it again.

One landmine remains in Deaf's message: he called my target "the third wire, the rightmost one." Rightmost is his left/right frame — the exact ambiguity that killed my pointed question, which he couldn't parse. But I no longer need him to answer left/right at all. My hands are a channel he can see: I'll grip the wire nearest the light and hold it. He sees my hand and that wire's color together; his next report naming the color of the wire I hold locks the anchor, and green's position follows by arithmetic from his fixed blue-red-green order. One observation resolves everything — and it doubles as the grip-confirmation he demanded, just starting from a deliberate anchor instead of a guess at "rightmost."

To Mute: alignment status, the calibration plan (Mute hears me directly and can flag any manual objection to touching wires before round 10), the round-by-round checksum, and silence otherwise. To Deaf, in his own five-sign code: here, agreed. No cut — round 11 is the only window, and the mapping isn't locked yet.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. I have Deaf's full relay: five-color cycle, yellow light means cut the green wire, blue white and red mean do nothing, the color at the exact moment of the cut is what counts, display zero is irrelevant, next yellow window is round eleven, GO cuts, ABORT freezes. I am aligned and I will not cut before round eleven. Three items. One, calibration: right now I am gripping the wire nearest the light module and holding it. Deaf can see my hand and that wire's color at the same time, so ask him to state aloud the color of the wire I am gripping. His one answer locks the whole mapping, because his color order blue red green plus my anchored end tells me exactly where the green wire sits under my fingers. Rounds eight and nine are backup slots for this. Two, safety: Deaf wants me gripping and holding a wire through round ten. His decode said no press hold or release procedure exists anywhere, so I read gripping as harmless. If the manual says anything against touching wires, get a warning to Deaf before round ten. Three, checksum: round seven blue, round eight white, round nine red, round ten purple, round eleven yellow. Your relay chain worked, nothing else is needed from you unless the manual objects. My updates stay short from here.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👍"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
